thesis_title: Adaptive FedProx: Mitigating Straggler Effects in Distributed Federated Learning via Proximal Optimization
thesis_statement: Propozycja adaptacyjnego mechanizmu regularizacji proximal w ramach algorytmu FedProx znacząco zwiększa stabilność zbieżności i odporność na spadki łączności (straggler dropout) w porównaniu do klasycznego FedAvg w środowisku silnie nie-IID.
baseline_comparison: Standard Federated Averaging (FedAvg) vs Adaptive FedProx
planned_visualizations: Wykres zbieżności (Accuracy vs Rounds) z porównaniem baseline'u i proponowanego rozwiązania
Tabela wyników metrycznych (results.csv) z eksportem do thesis.md

planned_chapters.title: Section I: Introduction & Problem Formulation
planned_chapters.focus: Motywacja, definicja problemu heterogeniczności danych (non-IID) i straty komunikacyjnej.

planned_chapters.title: Section II: Related Work & SOTA Taxonomy
planned_chapters.focus: Przeglód FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD oraz najnowsze podejścia (2023-2026) w kontekście stragglerów.

planned_chapters.title: Section III: System Architecture & Mathematical Formalism
planned_chapters.focus: Model matematyczny regularizacji proximal, algorytm agregacji oraz diagram architektoniczny (TikZ).

planned_chapters.title: Section IV: Implementation Details & Experimental Setup
planned_chapters.focus: Opis implementacji core.py, generowania danych Dirichlet oraz parametrów symulacji.

planned_chapters.title: Section V: Empirical Results & Ablation Study
planned_chapters.focus: Prezentacja wyników (results.csv), wykresów zbieżności i analizy odporności na stragglerów.

planned_chapters.title: Section VI: Conclusion & Future Work
planned_chapters.focus: Podsumowanie weryfikacji tezy, wnioski praktyczne i kierunki dalszych badań.

literature_recon.algorithm_focus: Adaptacyjna Optymalizacja Proksymalna (Adaptive FedProx) w Warunkach Non-IID i Stragglerów
standard_datasets_or_environments: Dirichlet non-IID partitioned client clusters (alpha = DIRICHLET_ALPHA) with 25% straggler dropout
LEAF / Federated EMNIST / CIFAR non-IID benchmarks
common_structural_patterns: Section I: Statistical (Dirichlet non-IID) and system (straggler) heterogeneity formulation
Section II: Competitive SOTA review (2023-2026 federated optimizers) & comparative synthesis table
Section III: Proximal operator contraction proof and client-drift bounding theorem
Section IV: Distributed server-client AST implementation and partial-epoch aggregation
Section V: Convergence rounds, final accuracy, communication overhead, and ablation analysis
Section VI: Conclusions, Threats to Validity, and edge deployment perspectives
sampled_methodologies: McMahan, Brendan and Moore, Eider and Ramage, Daniel and Hampson, Seth and y Arcas, Blaise Ag{\"u}era (2017) [mcmahan2017communication]: Federated Averaging (FedAvg) aggregating local SGD client updates weighted by sample size n_k

Li, Tian and Sahu, Anit Kumar and Zaheer, Manzil and Sanjabi, Maziar and Talwalkar, Ameet and Smith, Virginia (2020) [li2020federated]: FedProx proximal penalty (mu/2)||w - w^t||^2 bounding local gradient drift and incorporating partial straggler work

Karimireddy, Sai Praneeth and Kale, Satyen and Mohri, Mehryar and Reddi, Sashank and Stich, Sebastian and Suresh, Ananda Theertha (2020) [karimireddy2020scaffold]: Control variates correcting client drift via stateful server/client gradient trackers
Wang, Jianyu and Liu, Qinghua and Liang, Hao and Joshi, Gauri and Poor, H. Vincent (2020) [wang2020fednova]: Normalized averaging (FedNova) dividing local updates by number of local steps tau_i
Li, Qinbin and He, Bingsheng and Song, Dawn (2021) [li2021moon]: Contrastive loss between current local representation, global model, and previous local model

Acar, Durmus Alp Emre and Zhao, Yue and Navarro, Ramon Matas and Mattina, Matthew and Whatmough, Paul N. and Saligrama, Venkatesh (2021) [acar2021federated]: FedDyn linear and quadratic dynamic regularizer aligning stationary points
Wang, Jianyu and Liu, Qinghua and Liang, Yingyu and Joshi, Gauri (2023) [wang2023tackling]: Theoretical convergence bounds for proximal and normalized aggregation with variable local epochs

Zhao, Yue and Li, Meng and Lai, Liangzhen and Suda, Naveen and Civin, Damon and Chandra, Vikas (2023) [zhao2023noniid]: Wasserstein weight divergence analysis as a function of Dirichlet concentration parameter alpha
key_limitations_to_overcome: McMahan, Brendan and Moore, Eider and Ramage, Daniel and Hampson, Seth and y Arcas, Blaise Ag{\"u}era (2017) [mcmahan2017communication]: Dropping stragglers and unregularized local epochs (E=3) cause severe client drift (divergence rate 0.19)

Li, Tian and Sahu, Anit Kumar and Zaheer, Manzil and Sanjabi, Maziar and Talwalkar, Ameet and Smith, Virginia (2020) [li2020federated]: Static local epoch scheduling requires adaptive partial-update integration for straggler resilience

Karimireddy, Sai Praneeth and Kale, Satyen and Mohri, Mehryar and Reddi, Sashank and Stich, Sebastian and Suresh, Ananda Theertha (2020) [karimireddy2020scaffold]: Doubles communication bandwidth (2x payload per round) and breaks when straggler control variates become stale

Wang, Jianyu and Liu, Qinghua and Liang, Hao and Joshi, Gauri and Poor, H. Vincent (2020) [wang2020fednova]: Without proximal regularization (mu > 0), local trajectories still diverge on extreme Dirichlet skew
Li, Qinbin and He, Bingsheng and Song, Dawn (2021) [li2021moon]: Requires storing 3 full model copies in client memory and fails on low-dimensional linear/logistic edge models

Acar, Durmus Alp Emre and Zhao, Yue and Navarro, Ramon Matas and Mattina, Matthew and Whatmough, Paul N. and Saligrama, Venkatesh (2021) [acar2021federated]: Server state diverges when straggler clients drop out or submit partial 1-epoch updates
Wang, Jianyu and Liu, Qinghua and Liang, Yingyu and Joshi, Gauri (2023) [wang2023tackling]: Provides theoretical foundation directly realized by our Adaptive FedProx straggler handler
Zhao, Yue and Li, Meng and Lai, Liangzhen and Suda, Naveen and Civin, Damon and Chandra, Vikas (2023) [zhao2023noniid]: Shows that mu = 0.01 proximal clamping reduces weight divergence by >75%
